portedFrom: ts/packages/moq-core (this repository); the TypeScript snapshot is the reference implementation
adaptations: Ported from TypeScript to Python 3.11+ asyncio; module names are snake_case and the WHATWG stream seam becomes moq_core.transport.
Discriminated unions (control messages, location filters, fetch entries) are frozen dataclasses carrying a `kind`/`type` class attribute with the TypeScript spelling.
Varints cover the full 64-bit wire range because Python integers are exact; the TypeScript 2^53-1 ceiling and its guards are not needed.
Timers use the asyncio event loop; durations in the SDK API are seconds rather than milliseconds.
The default SETUP implementation identifier names moq-core (Python). The MoqtProtocolError type is the identity test for session-fatal codec errors.
Publish session extraction excludes the SPF actor and accepts explicit track properties instead of imposing the LOC microsecond timescale.

The subscribe session's close sends no GOAWAY, unlike the upstream driver's best-effort GOAWAY(0): one written as the transport closes gives the peer nothing to act on and the session has no drain to offer, and the publish session already sends none (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #128). Receiving GOAWAY is unchanged.

The publish session closes with INVALID_REQUEST_ID rather than PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when the peer reuses a request ID, and also when a peer request ID has the client's (even) parity, as draft-20 Section 10.1 requires. Tests that stand the subscribe driver in for the relay give it odd request IDs through a transport wrapper.

The publish session ends each Established subscription it ends with PUBLISH_DONE (a status, and a Stream Count of the data streams opened for it) after closing that subscription's data streams, then FIN, instead of the upstream FIN alone. `open_uni_stream(track_alias)` names the subscription a data stream serves, so the session can count it and reset it if still open. This needs moq-relay 0.15.4 or later (spec/behavior.md, "Relay interop deviations"; issue #TBD).
migration: Port of the initial extraction snapshot. Keep the two cores in lockstep through spec/; do not let the ports drift into separately maintained protocol implementations.
